Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.This is the second bail application.
First was disposed of on 21.3.2023 and relevant paragraph thereof is mentioned hereinafter:

" In the present case, victim is a minor girl who has lodged herself the F.I.R.
Statement of victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is very specific that applicant harassed her for last 2 years and committed rape.
The affidavit of mother of victim (sister of applicant) is not part of case diary, therefore, cannot be relied upon.

There is merit in argument of learned A.G.A.-I that considering the relationship of applicant with victim, in case of bail, it is very likelihood that he will try to influence her and till date statement of victim has not been recorded, therefore, at this stage,

sentences.text: However, this application is disposed of with a direction that learned trial Court shall take all endeavour to record statement of victim within a period of eight weeks from today, if there is no legal impediment and thereafter, applicant will have a liberty to file fresh bail application before learned trial Court.

"
2. The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.0177 of 2021, under Section 376 I.P.C.,
and under Section 5 (N)/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station-Nazirabad, District-Kanpur Nagar.
3.

In pursuance of an order passed by this Court, learned Trial Court has submitted a status report that out of proposed ten prosecution witnesses, three have already been examined including the victim as P.W.2 and trial could be concluded within a period of one year.

4. In the first round, Sri Manish Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant was not present,
therefore, this Court requested Ms. Samriddhi Upadhyaya, Advocate a young lawyer sitting in the Court to assist the Court.

5. When the matter was called after half an hour, learned counsel for the applicant was present However, the Court heard Ms.Samriddhi Upadhyaya, Advocate on behalf of applicant and at the first instance she submits that present applicant is related to victim as her real 'Mama' and it appears that he has found victim and her boy friend in a compromising position.
Victim has assaulted her boy friend.

She further submits that victim has supported the case of prosecution in her examination-in-chief however diluted the case of prosecution in her cross-examination to the extent that prosecution sought liberty to cross-examine her and that she has made a statement that no offence was committed by the applicant and she has made a complaint for the above referred reason as well as her mother was not inclined to repay the loan taken by the applicant.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has adopted the aforesaid submission.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 18.12.2021 i.e. more than two years.

Learned counsel for the applicant lastly submitted that there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial and the applicant undertakes that if enlarged on bail, he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.
8. Sri Mithilesh Kumar, learned A.G.A has opposed the bail application, but he has not been able to dispute the above nature of evidence on the basis of material on record.

9. I have considered the above mentioned rival submissions in referred factual and legal background and in view of established principle of jurisprudence of bail i.e 'bail is rule and jail is exception' as well as relevant factors for consideration of a bail application such as (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence; (ii) nature and gravity of the accusation; (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv) danger of Brijesh @ Bijesh vs State Of Up 3 Others on 16 April, 2024

2 the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means, position and standing of the accused;(vi) likelihood of the offence being repeated; (vii) reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being influenced; (viii) danger of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail etc. and that an order to grant or not to grant bail must assigned reasons (see Deepak Yadav Vs.
State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 559, Manoj Kumar Khokar Vs. State of Rajasthan and Anr (2022) 3 SCC 501, The State of Jharkhand Vs. Dhananjay Gupta @ Dhananjay Prasad Gupta: Order dated 7.11.2023 in SLP (Crl) No.10810/2023 and Shiv Kumar Vs The State of U.P. and Ors: Order dated 12.9.2023 in Criminal Appeal No.2782 of 2023), therefore, I am of considered opinion that present is a fit case to grant bail to applicant mainly on following reasons:-
(i) Applicant is in jail since 18.12.2021 i.e. more than 2 years and statement of victim has already been recorded, therefore, there is no chance to influence witnesses.

(ii) Applicant is related to victim as his 'Mama' and as referred above victim in her cross-examination has diluted the prosecution case and this Court takes note of the submission that possibility of conviction appears to be very remote.
10. Let the applicant- Brijesh @ Bijesh, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.

(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of the applicant, if there is no other legal impediment.

(v) Applicant has to appear on each and every date before learned Trial Court and any application for exemption of his appearance on vague ground could be a ground for cancellation of bail by learned Trial Court without even issuing notice.
